why: Collapses 'could not ask' into 'asked and was told no'. Both are `webgl2: false`, so a consumer that does not care keeps one branch and nothing about the gameplay decision changes -- which is what makes this silent. What it destroys is the cause issue #325's branded screen would render: a locked-down document, or a host whose `createElement`/`getContext` throws, gets blamed on the GPU. Anchored on the catch-site return by its leading newline and indentation, because the identical text also appears inside the `if (canvas == null)` return one line up and an unanchored find would be refused as ambiguous -- so this entry mutates the THROWN branch only. 2 of 14 in the scoped run: 'reports probe-failed, not no-webgl2, when getContext throws' and 'reports probe-failed when createElement itself throws'. The third `probe-failed` case, 'reports probe-failed when the host produces no canvas at all', returns from the un-mutated site one line up and keeps passing -- which is what shows this mutation is site-specific rather than that case failing as collateral. THAT site has its own entry, `render-capability-no-canvas-reads-as-no-webgl2`; the two are pinned separately because neither can stand in for the other. expectFailures counts that scoped run only. COUNT RE-MEASURED after PR #474's review fix: 2 -> 3. The new 'reading the default document throws' case routes to this same catch site, so it fails here too. The failing SET was compared, not the number renumbered.
